subject: english_sp7
source: Podstawa programowa kształcenia ogólnego dla szkoły podstawowej, język obcy nowożytny, wariant II.1 (klasy IV–VIII, pierwszy język; Dz.U. 2017 poz. 356, zm. Dz.U. 2024 poz. 996), wymaganie I (13 tematów leksykalnych i środki gramatyczne); dobór słownictwa na poziomie klasy 7

items.example: My brother is very tall.
She has long curly hair.
Our new neighbours are very friendly.
Don't be lazy and do your homework!
Tom is confident when he speaks in public.
I keep my clothes in the wardrobe.
The soup is on the cooker.
I do the washing-up after dinner.
Our neighbour has a big dog.
My favourite subject is biology.
Check the timetable before you go to school.
I hope to pass an exam in June.
He didn't study, so he will fail the test.
Doctors earn a lot of money.
The nurse works at the hospital.
She is happy with her salary.
My cousin lives in London.
I get on well with my sister.
We visit our grandparents every Sunday.
This pizza is really tasty.
Boil the water for the pasta.
Mum likes to fry fish.
Can I have a slice of bread?
My sister is vegetarian, so she doesn't eat meat.
These shoes are cheap.
The new phone is very expensive.
Keep the receipt in case you want to return it.
Can I try on this jacket?
Our luggage is in the car.
We need to book a hotel room.
We went sightseeing in Rome.
Don't forget your passport!
There is a new exhibition at the museum.
The audience loved the concert.
I am reading a novel by J.K. Rowling.
Our team wants to win the match.
The referee stopped the game.
I want to score a goal in the next match.
She took part in a swimming competition.
I have a terrible headache.
I can't sing because I have a sore throat.
Fruit and vegetables are healthy.
Take this medicine twice a day.
You can download the app for free.
Who invented the telephone?
The screen of my phone is broken.
We should protect the environment.
Air pollution is a big problem in cities.
We recycle paper and plastic.
The weather forecast says it will rain.
The police are investigating the crime.
She works as a volunteer at an animal shelter.
My grandma is very generous and always gives me presents.
He is so stubborn that he never changes his mind.
In summer she gets freckles on her nose.
Most teenagers spend a lot of time online.
I felt embarrassed when I forgot her name.
We live on the fifth floor of a block of flats.
There are old boxes in the attic.
My aunt lives in the suburbs of Warsaw.
Dad does the ironing on Sunday evenings.
Put your socks in the chest of drawers.
I have to revise for the history test tomorrow.
The teacher saw him cheat in the exam.
He got detention for being late again.
Chess club is one of the extracurricular activities at our school.
My brother wants to apply for a job in a café.
She has a part-time job at the weekend.
The nurse works the night shift this week.
The company has over two hundred employees.
I am an only child, so I have no brothers or sisters.
My stepfather is a great cook.
My cousin is going to get married in June.
I like to hang out with my friends after school.
I sometimes argue with my brother about the computer.
We celebrate my birthday with a big family dinner.
Let's order a takeaway instead of cooking tonight.
For the starter I would like tomato soup.
This curry is too spicy for me.
These trainers were a real bargain in the sale.
The shop gave me a refund because the T-shirt was damaged.
These jeans don't fit me, they are too small.
You can buy almost anything in a department store.
There is a two-hour delay on our flight.
The train to Kraków leaves from platform 3.
We found cheap accommodation near the beach.
We got lost in the old town without a map.
A return ticket to London costs forty pounds.
There is a famous sculpture in the park.
The plot of the film was really exciting.
The band will perform at the festival on Saturday.
Decorating the Christmas tree is a family tradition.
Poland beat Germany two-nil last night.
Our coach makes us run five kilometres every day.
The football pitch was wet after the rain.
He can't play because of a knee injury.
I have had a bad cough for a week.
You need a prescription for these tablets.
I cycle to school to keep fit.
A smartwatch is a small device that you wear on your wrist.
Can I borrow your phone charger?
We did an experiment with magnets in the science lab.
Never tell anyone your password.
The drought destroyed the farmers' crops.
After the storm there was a flood in the village.
The panda is an endangered species.
We spent the weekend in the countryside.

items.text: Listen! Somebody {{is singing}} in the garden.
items.explanation: Czynność dziejąca się teraz: am/is/are + -ing.

items.text: Yesterday we {{went}} to the cinema with our class.
items.explanation: Czasownik nieregularny: go – went – gone.

items.text: I have lived in this town {{since}} 2015.
items.explanation: Present Perfect: since + punkt w czasie (2015), for + okres (ten years).

items.text: Mount Everest is {{the highest}} mountain in the world.
items.explanation: Stopień najwyższy krótkich przymiotników: the + -est.

items.text: If it rains tomorrow, we {{will stay}} at home.
items.explanation: First conditional: if + Present Simple, will + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Harry Potter {{was written}} by J.K. Rowling.
items.hint: write; strona bierna w Past Simple
items.explanation: Strona bierna: was/were + trzecia forma czasownika (written).

items.text: Emma: 'I have a headache.' → Yesterday Emma said that she {{had}} a headache.
items.explanation: Po said w czasie przeszłym Present Simple zmienia się na Past Simple.

items.text: Dad: 'I'm making soup.' → Dad said that he {{was making}} soup.
items.explanation: Po said Present Continuous zmienia się na Past Continuous.

items.text: Zoe: 'I have lost my appetite.' → Zoe told the doctor that she {{had lost}} her appetite.
items.explanation: Present Perfect zmienia się na Past Perfect (had + III forma).

items.text: Liam: 'I will text you later.' → Liam said that he {{would}} text me later.
items.explanation: Czasownik modalny will zmienia się w mowie zależnej na would.

items.text: Mia: 'I saw the doctor yesterday.' → Mia said that she had seen the doctor {{the day before / the previous day}}.
items.explanation: Okoliczniki czasu przesuwają się razem z relacją: yesterday → the day before.

items.text: Jack: 'I'll visit you tomorrow.' → Jack said that he would visit me {{the next day / the following day}}.
items.explanation: W mowie zależnej tomorrow zmienia się na the next day / the following day.

items.text: Nurse: 'Do you take any medicine?' → The nurse asked me {{if I took / whether I took}} any medicine.
items.explanation: Pytanie yes/no relacjonujemy przez if/whether, szyk zdania oznajmującego i backshift (Present Simple → Past Simple).

items.text: Tom: 'Where is the chemist's?' → Tom asked me where {{the chemist's was}}.
items.explanation: W pytaniu zależnym podmiot stoi przed czasownikiem, bez inwersji; is → was (backshift).

items.text: Doctor: 'Don't eat nuts.' → The doctor told me {{not to eat}} nuts.
items.explanation: Polecenia relacjonujemy przez tell + osoba + (not) to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Jake: 'I'm sorry I'm late.' → Jake apologised {{for being}} late.
items.explanation: Po czasowniku relacjonującym apologise stoi for + -ing.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'tomorrow' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Okoliczniki czasu przesuwają się razem z czasem relacji: tomorrow → the next day / the following day.

items.question: Po którym czasowniku relacjonującym zawsze stoi osoba (… me, … us)?
items.explanation: Tell wymaga dopełnienia: told me that…; say go nie wymaga: said (to me) that….

items.example: Kate promised to bring my book back on Monday.
The nurse advised me to drink more water.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Anna: 'I will call you tomorrow.'
items.answer: Anna said (that) she would call me the next day.
accept: Anna said she would call me the next day.
Anna said that she would call me the following day.
Anna said she would call me the following day.
items.explanation: will → would, you → me, tomorrow → the next day / the following day.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Mum: 'Don't forget your inhaler.'
items.answer: Mum told me not to forget my inhaler.
accept: Mum told me not to forget the inhaler.
items.explanation: Zakaz: tell + osoba + not to + bezokolicznik; your → my.

items.text: Ben: 'I don't like hospitals.' → Ben said that he {{didn't like}} hospitals.
items.explanation: Po said Present Simple zmienia się na Past Simple, także w przeczeniu: don't → didn't.

items.text: Sara: 'We are at the clinic.' → Sara said that they {{were}} at the clinic.
items.explanation: Present Simple (are) zmienia się na Past Simple (were); we → they.

items.text: Kate: 'I'm waiting for the nurse.' → Kate said that she {{was waiting}} for the nurse.
items.explanation: Po said Present Continuous zmienia się na Past Continuous.

items.text: Max: 'I broke my arm last winter.' → Max told us that he {{had broken}} his arm the winter before.
items.explanation: Po told Past Simple zmienia się na Past Perfect (had + III forma).

items.text: Olivia: 'I took the tablets at 8.' → Olivia said that she {{had taken}} the tablets at 8.
items.explanation: Past Simple (took) zmienia się na Past Perfect (had taken).

items.text: Noah: 'I've never had food poisoning.' → Noah said that he {{had never had}} food poisoning.
items.explanation: Present Perfect (have had) zmienia się na Past Perfect (had had).

items.text: Lucy: 'I can't walk without crutches.' → Lucy said that she {{couldn't}} walk without crutches.
items.explanation: Czasownik modalny can zmienia się na could (can't → couldn't).

items.text: Dr Lee: 'The results will be ready on Friday.' → Dr Lee said the results {{would}} be ready on Friday.
items.explanation: Czasownik modalny will zmienia się na would.

items.text: Mum: 'You may need an X-ray.' → Mum said that I {{might}} need an X-ray.
items.explanation: Czasownik modalny may zmienia się na might; you → I.

items.text: Nurse: 'You must stay in bed.' → The nurse said that I {{had to}} stay in bed.
items.explanation: Czasownik modalny must zmienia się w mowie zależnej na had to.

items.text: Jo: 'I'm going to see a doctor.' → Jo said that she {{was going to}} see a doctor.
items.explanation: Konstrukcja am/is going to zmienia się na was going to.

items.text: Tim: 'You should drink more water.' → Tim said that I {{should}} drink more water.
items.explanation: Czasowniki modalne should, would, could, might nie zmieniają się w mowie zależnej.

items.text: Amy: 'I could help you with the bandage.' → Amy said that she {{could}} help me with the bandage.
items.explanation: Could nie zmienia się w mowie zależnej (jak would, might, should).

items.text: Leo: 'I had already eaten.' → Leo said that he {{had already eaten}}.
items.explanation: Past Perfect zostaje bez zmiany, bo nie ma już wcześniejszego czasu.

items.text: Ella says: 'I am allergic to nuts.' → Ella says that she {{is}} allergic to nuts.
items.explanation: Gdy czasownik relacjonujący jest w Present Simple (says), nie ma backshiftu.

items.text: Teacher: 'Water boils at 100 degrees.' → The teacher said that water {{boils / boiled}} at 100 degrees.
items.explanation: Prawdy ogólne można zostawić w Present Simple, backshift też jest poprawny.

items.text: Doctor: 'Smoking is bad for your lungs.' → The doctor said that smoking {{is / was}} bad for your lungs.
items.explanation: Fakt, który nadal jest prawdziwy, może zostać w Present Simple; Past Simple też jest poprawny.

items.question: Po jakim czasie czasownika relacjonującego (says, tells) nie ma backshiftu?
items.explanation: She says (that) she is ill: po czasowniku relacjonującym w Present Simple czas zdania zostaje bez zmian.

items.question: Jakie zdania można zostawić bez backshiftu nawet po said?
items.explanation: Prawdy ogólne i fakty nadal prawdziwe (The Earth goes round the Sun) mogą zostać w Present Simple po said.

items.text: Anna: 'I have lost my inhaler.' → Anna said that {{she}} had lost her inhaler.
items.explanation: Zaimek I zmienia się na he/she zgodnie z osobą, która mówiła.

items.text: Olivia: 'I can't find my glasses.' → Olivia said that she couldn't find {{her}} glasses.
items.explanation: Określnik my zmienia się na his/her zgodnie z osobą mówiącą; can't → couldn't.

items.text: Mark: 'We are going to the pool.' → Mark told me that {{they}} were going to the pool.
items.explanation: Zaimek we zmienia się na they, gdy relacjonuje osoba spoza grupy.

items.text: Dad: 'You look tired.' → Dad told me that {{I}} looked tired.
items.explanation: Zaimek you zmienia się na I/me, gdy relacjonuje osoba, do której mówiono.

items.text: Sam: 'This medicine tastes awful.' → Sam said that {{that}} medicine tasted awful.
items.explanation: Określnik this zmienia się w mowie zależnej na that (these → those).

items.question: Na co zmienia się 'this' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: This → that, these → those: 'I like this song' → she said she liked that song.

items.text: Mia: 'I feel dizzy now.' → Mia said that she felt dizzy {{then / at that time}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik now zmienia się na then / at that time.

items.text: Ben: 'I have an appointment today.' → Ben said that he had an appointment {{that day}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik today zmienia się na that day.

items.text: Kate: 'I hurt my knee two days ago.' → Kate said that she had hurt her knee two days {{before / earlier}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik ago zmienia się na before / earlier.

items.text: Tom: 'The chemist's is here.' → Tom said that the chemist's was {{there}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik miejsca here zmienia się na there.

items.text: Zoe: 'I had the flu last week.' → Zoe said that she had had the flu {{the week before / the previous week}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik last week zmienia się na the week before / the previous week.

items.text: Dr Shah: 'We'll check your eyes next month.' → Dr Shah said they would check my eyes {{the following month / the next month}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik next month zmienia się na the following month / the next month.

items.text: Lily: 'I can't sleep tonight.' → Lily said that she couldn't sleep {{that night}}.
items.explanation: Okolicznik tonight zmienia się na that night.

items.text: Jack: 'I was here yesterday.' → Jack said that he {{had been there}} the day before.
items.explanation: Past Simple → Past Perfect (was → had been) i here → there.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'yesterday' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Okoliczniki czasu przesuwają się razem z czasem relacji: yesterday → the day before.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'now' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Now → then / at that time: 'I'm busy now' → he said he was busy then.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'today' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Today → that day: 'I'm ill today' → she said she was ill that day.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'ago' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Ago → before / earlier: 'two days ago' → two days before.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'here' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Okolicznik miejsca here → there: 'Wait here' → she told me to wait there.

items.question: Jak zmienia się 'last week' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Last week → the week before / the previous week (tak samo last month, last year).

items.text: Mum: 'Your appointment is at five.' → Mum {{told}} me that my appointment was at five.
items.explanation: Przed osobą (me, us, him) stoi tell: told me that…; say łączy się z osobą tylko przez to.

items.text: Jake: 'I'm feeling better.' → Jake {{said}} that he was feeling better.
items.explanation: Bez osoby używamy say: said (that)…; tell zawsze wymaga osoby (told me that…).

items.text: Lena said {{to me}} that she had hay fever.
items.explanation: Say łączy się z osobą tylko przez to: said to me; 'said me' to typowy błąd.

items.question: Jak powiedzieć 'powiedziała mi' z czasownikiem say?
items.explanation: Say + to + osoba: she said to me that…; bez to używamy tell: she told me that….

items.question: Które słowo po said / told można pominąć?
items.explanation: Spójnik that jest opcjonalny: she said (that) she was tired.

items.text: Doctor: 'Does it hurt?' → The doctor asked me {{if it hurt / whether it hurt}}.
items.explanation: Pytanie yes/no: if/whether + szyk zdania oznajmującego, bez does, z backshiftem (hurt).

items.text: Mum: 'Are you feeling better?' → Mum asked me {{if I was feeling / whether I was feeling}} better.
items.explanation: Pytanie yes/no: if/whether, podmiot przed czasownikiem, Present Continuous → Past Continuous.

items.text: Liam: 'What time does the clinic open?' → Liam asked what time the clinic {{opened}}.
items.explanation: W pytaniu zależnym znika does, a czasownik dostaje Past Simple (backshift).

items.text: Teacher: 'Why are you late?' → The teacher asked me why {{I was}} late.
items.explanation: W pytaniu zależnym nie ma inwersji: podmiot (I) przed czasownikiem (was).

items.text: Dad: 'Where did you put the thermometer?' → Dad asked me where {{I had put}} the thermometer.
items.explanation: W pytaniu zależnym znika did, a Past Simple zmienia się na Past Perfect; podmiot przed czasownikiem.

items.text: Sam: 'Can I borrow your bike?' → Sam asked me {{if he could / whether he could}} borrow my bike.
items.explanation: Pytanie yes/no: if + podmiot + could (can → could), bez inwersji.

items.text: Mum: 'How often do you take the tablets?' → Mum wanted to know how often I {{took}} the tablets.
items.explanation: Po wanted to know pytanie wh- ma szyk zdania oznajmującego, bez do, z backshiftem (take → took).

items.text: Ella: 'Is the pool open on Sundays?' → Ella wondered {{whether / if}} the pool was open on Sundays.
items.explanation: Po wonder / ask / want to know pytanie yes/no wprowadza if lub whether.

items.question: Jakim słowem wprowadzamy pytanie yes/no w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Pytanie yes/no: asked if/whether + zdanie w szyku oznajmującym.

items.question: Jaki szyk ma pytanie zależne (po asked where / asked if)?
items.explanation: Pytanie zależne ma szyk zdania oznajmującego: asked where I lived, nie 'where did I live'.

items.question: Co znika z pytania w mowie zależnej: 'Do you like it?' → asked if I liked it?
items.explanation: Czasownik posiłkowy do/does/did znika, a czas przechodzi na główny czasownik (liked).

items.question: Jakim znakiem kończy się pytanie zależne (He asked where I lived)?
items.explanation: Pytanie zależne jest zdaniem oznajmującym, więc kończy się kropką, nie znakiem zapytania.

items.text: Coach: 'Warm up before the match.' → The coach told us {{to warm up}} before the match.
items.explanation: Polecenie: tell + osoba + to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Grandma: 'Could you carry my bag, please?' → Grandma {{asked me to carry}} her bag.
items.explanation: Prośbę (Could you…, please?) relacjonujemy przez ask + osoba + to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Nurse: 'Please don't move your arm.' → The nurse asked me {{not to move}} my arm.
items.explanation: Prośba przecząca: ask + osoba + not to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Teacher: 'Sit down and open your books.' → The teacher ordered us {{to sit}} down and open our books.
items.explanation: Po order / tell + osoba stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Lifeguard: 'Don't swim near the rocks!' → The lifeguard warned us {{not to swim}} near the rocks.
items.explanation: Zakaz po warn: warn + osoba + not to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Jo: 'Can you text me the address?' → Jo asked {{me to text}} her the address.
items.explanation: Po ask zawsze stoi osoba, a potem to + bezokolicznik: asked me to text.

items.text: Mum: 'Don't go there.' → Mum told me {{not to go}} there.
items.explanation: Zakaz: tell + osoba + not to + bezokolicznik; 'to not go' to typowy błąd.

items.question: Jak relacjonujemy polecenie 'Sit down!'? She told me ___
items.explanation: Polecenie: tell + osoba + to + bezokolicznik: she told me to sit down.

items.question: Jak relacjonujemy zakaz 'Don't do it!'? He told me ___ it
items.explanation: Zakaz: tell + osoba + not to + bezokolicznik; nie 'to not do'.

items.question: Którym czasownikiem relacjonujemy prośbę ('Can you help me, please?')?
items.explanation: Prośby relacjonujemy przez ask + osoba + to; tell to polecenie, a say nie łączy się z to + bezokolicznik.

items.example: Dan offered to carry my bag to the bus stop.
Jake refused to lend me his bike.
Mum agreed to drive us to the match.
Liz suggested going to the pool after school.
The doctor recommended drinking more water.
Tom admitted breaking the window.
Ola apologised for forgetting my birthday.

items.word: warn sb not to do sth
polish: ostrzec kogoś, żeby czegoś nie robił
items.example: The nurse warned me not to scratch the rash.
Dad reminded me to take my inhaler.
Zoe invited me to stay at her house.
My coach encouraged me to try climbing.
The doctor explained that the rash was an allergy.
Ben complained that his leg still hurt.

items.text: Dan: 'I'll carry your bag.' → Dan offered {{to carry}} my bag.
items.explanation: Po offer stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Jake: 'No, I won't lend you my bike.' → Jake refused {{to lend}} me his bike.
items.explanation: Po refuse stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Mum: 'OK, I'll drive you to the match.' → Mum agreed {{to drive}} us to the match.
items.explanation: Po agree stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Kate: 'I promise I'll call you.' → Kate promised {{to call}} me.
items.explanation: Po promise stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Liz: 'Let's go to the pool.' → Liz suggested {{going}} to the pool.
items.explanation: Po suggest stoi czasownik z -ing, nigdy to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Doctor: 'You should drink more water.' → The doctor recommended {{drinking}} more water.
items.explanation: Po recommend stoi czasownik z -ing.

items.text: Tom: 'Yes, I broke the window.' → Tom admitted {{breaking}} the window.
items.explanation: Po admit stoi czasownik z -ing.

items.text: Nurse: 'Don't scratch the rash!' → The nurse warned me {{not to scratch}} the rash.
items.explanation: Po warn + osoba stoi (not) to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Dad: 'Remember to take your inhaler.' → Dad reminded me {{to take}} my inhaler.
items.explanation: Po remind + osoba stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Zoe: 'Would you like to stay at my house?' → Zoe invited me {{to stay}} at her house.
items.explanation: Po invite + osoba stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Coach: 'Go on, try climbing!' → My coach encouraged me {{to try}} climbing.
items.explanation: Po encourage + osoba stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.text: Doctor: 'The rash is an allergy.' → The doctor explained {{that}} the rash was an allergy.
items.explanation: Po explain stoi that + zdanie; 'explained me that' to typowy błąd (poprawnie: explained to me).

items.text: Ben: 'My leg still hurts.' → Ben complained {{that}} his leg still hurt.
items.explanation: Po complain stoi that + zdanie (albo about + rzeczownik).

items.text: Nurse: 'You should rest.' → The nurse advised me {{to rest}}.
items.explanation: Po advise + osoba stoi to + bezokolicznik.

items.question: Jaki wzorzec ma 'suggest'? suggest + ?
items.explanation: Suggest + -ing: she suggested going home; nigdy 'suggested to go'.

items.question: Jaki wzorzec ma 'remind'? remind + ?
items.explanation: Remind + osoba + to + bezokolicznik: he reminded me to call.

items.question: Jaki wzorzec ma 'apologise'? apologise + ?
items.explanation: Apologise for + -ing: she apologised for being late.

items.question: Popraw błąd: 'He said me that he was ill.'
accept: He told me that he was ill.
He said to me that he was ill.
items.explanation: Say nie łączy się bezpośrednio z osobą: told me that… albo said to me that….

items.question: Popraw błąd: 'She asked me where was the hospital.'
accept: She asked me where the hospital was.
items.explanation: Pytanie zależne ma szyk zdania oznajmującego: where the hospital was.

items.question: Popraw błąd: 'She said she would come tomorrow.' (relacja kilka dni później)
items.explanation: Okolicznik tomorrow zmienia się na the next day / the following day.

items.question: Popraw błąd: 'He asked if did I like sport.'
accept: He asked if I liked sport.
He asked whether I liked sport.
items.explanation: W pytaniu zależnym znika did, a czasownik ma Past Simple: if I liked.

items.question: Na jaki czas zmienia się Present Simple w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: 'I live here' → she said she lived there.

items.question: Na jaki czas zmienia się Past Simple w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: 'I saw it' → he said he had seen it.

items.question: Na jaki czas zmienia się Present Perfect w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: 'I have finished' → she said she had finished.

items.question: Który czas NIE zmienia się w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Past Perfect zostaje bez zmiany: 'I had left' → he said he had left.

items.question: Na co zmienia się 'can' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Can → could: 'I can swim' → she said she could swim.

items.question: Na co zmienia się 'will' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Will → would: 'I will help' → he said he would help.

items.question: Na co zmienia się 'must' w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Must → had to: 'You must rest' → the doctor said I had to rest.

items.question: Który czasownik modalny NIE zmienia się w mowie zależnej?
items.explanation: Would, could, might, should, ought to zostają bez zmiany; zmieniają się will, can, may, must.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Tom: 'I am tired.'
accept: Tom said that he was tired.
items.explanation: Present Simple → Past Simple (am → was), I → he.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Kate: 'I have never been to London.'
items.answer: Kate said (that) she had never been to London.
accept: Kate said she had never been to London.
Kate said that she had never been to London.
items.explanation: Present Perfect → Past Perfect (have been → had been), I → she.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Dad: 'Where are you going?'
items.answer: Dad asked me where I was going.
accept: Dad asked where I was going.
items.explanation: Pytanie wh-: szyk oznajmujący (I was), Present Continuous → Past Continuous, you → I.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Nurse: 'Do you have a temperature?'
items.answer: The nurse asked me if I had a temperature.
accept: The nurse asked if I had a temperature.
The nurse asked me whether I had a temperature.
The nurse asked whether I had a temperature.
items.explanation: Pytanie yes/no: if/whether, bez do, Present Simple → Past Simple (have → had).

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Teacher: 'Open your books, please.'
items.answer: The teacher asked us to open our books.
accept: The teacher told us to open our books.
items.explanation: Prośba: ask + osoba + to + bezokolicznik; your → our.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Mum: 'I can't drive you to school today.'
items.answer: Mum said (that) she couldn't drive me to school that day.
accept: Mum said she couldn't drive me to school that day.
Mum said that she couldn't drive me to school that day.
items.explanation: can't → couldn't, you → me, today → that day.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Ben: 'I saw this film last week.'
items.answer: Ben said (that) he had seen that film the week before.
accept: Ben said he had seen that film the week before.
Ben said that he had seen that film the previous week.
Ben said he had seen that film the previous week.
items.explanation: Past Simple → Past Perfect, this → that, last week → the week before / the previous week.

items.question: Przekształć w mowę zależną: Coach: 'Don't be late for training tomorrow.'
items.answer: The coach told us not to be late for training the next day.
accept: The coach told us not to be late for training the following day.
The coach told me not to be late for training the next day.
The coach told me not to be late for training the following day.
items.explanation: Zakaz: tell + osoba + not to + bezokolicznik; tomorrow → the next day / the following day.
